content: Th-Thanks... The expedition equipment and my protective gear are all just too heavy. When they designed this extreme north exploration gear, they probably didn't think we'd need to run in the mountains...

content: The Director always tells me to think before I act, but... Maybe it's because I have no idea what's so scary about these hallucinations, but I didn't really think that through, did I?

content: No need to apologize.

raw: [name="Typhon"]Nature doesn't debate right and wrong. All that matters is closeness. The same goes for those northern warriors just now.
speaker: Typhon
content: Nature doesn't debate right and wrong. All that matters is closeness. The same goes for those northern warriors just now.

speaker: Magallan
content: Uh... closeness...?

speaker: Typhon
content: They're just like, mm... like a chain of mountains. No matter what you say to them, you will never become part of the mountains. All you can do is try your hardest to surmount them.

content: Of course, you also can't tell the mountains that they're wrong and should be flat ground instead.

content: Ehh?

content: Why are they so unwilling to talk it out?

speaker: Typhon
content: Let's set aside whether they could even understand you. Those warriors normally have no need for words.

speaker: Typhon
content: See, if you and I lived together all day, every day, and everything we did was the same daily routine: patrolling, hunting, fighting... We wouldn't have much reason to talk.

content: Hm, because we'd be too used to everything?

speaker: Typhon
content: No. Because communication is only needed when we think different thoughts.

raw: [name="Typhon"]That's why I called them a chain of mountains.
speaker: Typhon
content: That's why I called them a chain of mountains.

speaker: Santalla
content: Besides, they have to deal with the Ursus, too.

raw: [name="Santalla"]To them, they must be wary of any outlanders whose intentions they cannot discern at a single glance.
speaker: Santalla
content: To them, they must be wary of any outlanders whose intentions they cannot discern at a single glance.

raw: [name="Santalla"]It may seem a little cruel, but it's how they have to live... (In Sami) 'One must accept fate, no matter what form it takes.'

content: It may seem a little cruel, but it's how they have to live... (In Sami) 'One must accept fate, no matter what form it takes.'

content: (In Sami) Fate... hm.

raw: [name="Typhon"]What's done is done. The signal I gave back there was for Simone to run. When you're dealing with those warriors, most of the time you're going to have to back down. You can't count on them giving way.
speaker: Typhon
content: What's done is done. The signal I gave back there was for Simone to run. When you're dealing with those warriors, most of the time you're going to have to back down. You can't count on them giving way.

content: That said, now we can't reach the icefield to find your teacher.

content: *sigh* Yeah...

speaker: Typhon
content: So what are you going to do now?

content: I guess... I'll go to Čappat to request help.

content: That's the southernmost city in Sami, isn't it?

content: Yeah, it's where a lot of Columbian companies have their only branch offices in Sami.

content: Now that the Ursus route is sealed off, it's the only place the Exploration Society can mount a rescue from.

content: I'll rendezvous with them and try my best to collect information on the route. After all, nobody's really all that familiar with Sami.

content: I'll keep escorting you, then.

speaker: Typhon
content: I don't need payment. I have no use for most of the trinkets southerners offer. I just happen to have a client waiting for me in Čappat.

content: I promised I'd stay with you, didn't I?

content: But Typhon, where does this path lead?

content: I find it hard to imagine that there are still paths in this mountain that the scouts haven't discovered.

content: That's because this takes us to where Arges lives.

content: Yeah, I guess it's my home, too. At least, I grew up there.

content: I may have used Sarkaz Arts to cover our tracks, but any veteran shaman is bound to figure it out in an instant. But I doubt they'd want to disturb a Cyclops.

content: Heh, no one likes hearing the prophesized tragedies doomed to befall them, after all.
